input.quote: 14.3 Choice of Law; Arbitration; Venue. This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of California, USA, excluding conflict of laws provisions and excluding the 1980 United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods. Any disputes arising out of this Agreement shall be resolved by binding arbitration in accordance with the then-current commercial arbitration rules of the American Arbitration Association ("RULES"). The arbitration shall be conducted by one (1) arbitrator appointed in accordance with the Rules in San Francisco County, California.
input.rationale: Section 14.3 is the sole governing law/venue provision (Section 12 escrow disputes are simply referred back to it). Governing law is California, which sits squarely within the playbook's fallback list (Delaware or California law and courts), rather than the preferred New York position. Disputes go to single-arbitrator AAA arbitration seated in San Francisco County, California, with judgment enforceable in the California courts — a domestic seat in the same accepted jurisdiction, not the walk-away scenario of a foreign venue or arbitration seated abroad. The use of arbitration instead of pure court litigation is a sub-element short of the preferred wording and is noted rather than redlined, particularly as a local California seat is convenient for us and the fee-shifting allocation is even-handed. Clause sits at the fallback and is acceptable.
